label: D1 after a rewarded a2->S2 (common) trial, mid-episode (trials ~30-89)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), only when the reward input is 1, and essentially only when the previous trial was a2 that reached S2 via a common transition (prev_action==1 or rare a2->S1 almost never fire). It is also gated by episode time: zero activity before episode trial ~25 and after ~89, which accounts for most false positives of the simpler predicate (F1 0.64 without the time window, 0.91 with it on dev). On the window first trial prev_action is unknown to the variables, so the agent own upcoming choice (action==2, a stay) is used as a proxy there; this is the only use of a FUTURE variable and it is the agent own computed choice, not a random outcome. Equivalent fully-observed form (prev_action in [2,-1]) gives recall 0.99 but precision 0.62. Activations are associated with a strongly a2-leaning policy (choice logit -4.4..-1.5) and mid-range value; magnitude is fairly uniform across activation quartiles of the predicate (coverage ~0.98-1.0), so no strong magnitude modulator was identified. Does not fire after unrewarded trials, after a1 choices, or after rare transitions.

issues: The checkable claims hold. On dev, 100% of activation mass is at D1, with zero activations at GO or D2. It fires only when in_rew == 1 (zero activations at in_rew 0 or -1). Activations at prev_action == 1 hold 0.3% of the mass. Rare a2->S1 rewarded gives P = 0.000 over 10409 predicted steps. a1->S2 rewarded gives P = 0.055. a2->S2 rewarded with ep_trial in 30-89 gives P = 0.859.

The time-window edges are softer and narrower than stated. Precision of the predicate by 2-trial episode bins: 28-29: 0.03, 30-31: 0.24, 32-33: 0.63, 36-37: 0.90, 40-81: about 0.97, 84-85: 0.56, 86-87: 0.16, 88-89: 0.02. So 'silent before ~25' is loose: it is essentially silent until about trial 30 and only reliable from about 34 on. Most of the predicate's remaining false positives sit at the 30-33 and 84-89 edges. Tightening the window to [32, 86) raises test F1 from 0.911 to 0.945 (P 0.922, R 0.970, mass recall 0.993).

The one FUTURE variable is used legitimately. On the window's first trial, (action == 2) stands in for the unknown previous trial: P = 0.81 with it versus 0.42 without it. After a rewarded common a2 trial the agent almost always stays (only 9 cases of a switch to a1), so action == 2 acts as a proxy for 'the previous choice was a2'. The observed-only version is clearly worse, as the other agent reported: test F1 0.846 with the [32, 86) window.

Minor and not systematic: after a rewarded a2->S2 trial whose own choice was a switch from a1 (tv('action', -2) == 1), precision falls to 0.46. If the trial before that was also a2, precision is 0.996. These cases are rare (recall share 0.005), so this is scattered noise, not a gap.

The feature does not track the hidden good state. Within the predicate it fires with P = 0.84 when good == S1 (shortly after reversals) and P = 0.85 when good == S2. It goes with the a2 history, not with S2 being good. The policy-logit (-4.4 to -1.5) and mid-range value correlations check out: no activations when value < 5.22, and only 3 predicted steps with choice < -4.44.
